title: Evaluation and functoriality of component-lift sections
statement: For every commutative condensed ring Lambda, all schemes U,V,W and all morphisms g:V→U and h:W→V, ComponentLiftSectionIdentity Lambda g and ComponentLiftSectionNaturality Lambda g [def-sfb-component-lift-section-data] hold. For every internal Lambda_T-module L, componentLiftHomSection Lambda T L is bijective. The section map for id_T becomes the identity under upperStarId. The section maps satisfy ComponentLiftSectionComposition Lambda g h under the specified upperStarComp. There are no lisseness, affineness, component-space, or contractibility assumptions. This asserts evaluation and the exact naturality, identity and composition formulas, without asserting that section pullback itself is bijective.

proof.text: The fully faithful singleFunctor identifies each derived Hom between degree-zero complexes with ordinary module Hom. A map t from the regular coefficient module to L is determined by the section s=t_T(1); at a test W it sends r to r times the restriction of s. Conversely this formula defines a module map, compatible with every restriction. These two constructions are inverse, proving bijectivity of componentLiftHomSection for every T and L. Naturality of the module adjunction unit with respect to t, and the mate relation of the coefficient map, identify the adjoint of the pullback of t with t followed by this unit. Evaluation at one therefore gives precisely the section map defined by the module unit followed by terminal base-change restriction. The single-functor comparison of the exact derived pullback is the displayed ComponentLiftSectionIdentity. This statement concerns the specified maps and asserts no bijectivity of section pullback.

proof.text: For a module morphism L→Lprime, naturality of the adjunction unit and the restriction square of the underlying sheaf morphism give ComponentLiftSectionNaturality. For W→V→U the unit of the composite adjunction is the unit for g followed by g_* of the unit for h. The canonical module composition isomorphism is the adjunction mate of the pushforward composition, so evaluating this unit equality at the terminal tests gives ComponentLiftSectionComposition under upperStarComp. The identity adjunction similarly gives the identity equation under upperStarId. For empty schemes all the same unit and naturality formulas remain valid; no coefficient discreteness, completeness, rank, connectedness or t-admissibility assumption has been used.

lean.statement:
theorem component_lift_section_normalization
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X] :
    (∀ (U V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U),
      ComponentLiftSectionIdentity Λ g ∧ ComponentLiftSectionNaturality Λ g) ∧
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u})
      (L : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X T)),
      Function.Bijective (componentLiftHomSection Λ T L)) ∧
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u})
      (L : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X T))
      (s : (condensedModuleSections Λ.X T).obj L),
      (condensedModuleSections Λ.X T).map ((upperStarId Λ.X T).hom.app L)
        ((componentLiftSectionPullback Λ (𝟙 T) L) s) = s) ∧
    (∀ (U V W : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U) (h : W ⟶ V),
      ComponentLiftSectionComposition Λ g h)
